takeaway: Slightly quieter Sunday locally: Costa Rica’s weather service sees a partial humidity dip and more isolated afternoon showers across Pacífico Norte, with Nicoya heat still sharp (around 35°C). Surf winds stay mostly Pacific/onshore — a light morning easterly near Papagayo today is not all-day glass, then flow trends south to southwest into midweek; a brief weak easterly window may return around Wednesday mornings. Distant East Pacific storms stay well away; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a very high (~90%) chance of forming within a week and should drift west-northwest along Mexico. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only, with a midweek–weekend wetter pulse possible but not a locked washout.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun–Tue)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service calls Sunday partly cloudy with possible scattered coastal showers in the morning, then scattered afternoon showers and rains across Pacífico Norte; nights stay mostly cloudy. Nicoya heat remains sharp (around 35°C). Compared with the sticky weekend setup, Sunday guidance leans a bit more isolated after a partial humidity reduction over southern Central America. Weekly outlook still expects humid Pacific inflow building again from Thursday toward next weekend, with early coastal rains possible then and no tropical waves crossing the next few days. Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate (typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine) through Tuesday, with U.S./European means and the AI ensemble broadly agreeing; European mean tends lightest early. Official longer outlook still keeps northern Pacific on the drier-than-normal side this week into next (roughly 1–70 mm Pacífico Norte for 5–11 Oct). Near-surface Papagayo: Sunday morning light northeasterly to easterly about 10 kt, overnight southeast, Monday south about 10–15 kt, then southeast to south Monday night into Tuesday.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before scattered afternoon storms; sticky air continues. For surf, treat Sunday–Tuesday as mostly Pacific/onshore–side days: today’s light Papagayo easterly is brief and light, not glassy all-day offshore. Early checks only.
periods.confidence: High that Sunday–Tuesday stay moist Pacific-side days with scattered storms and no nearby cyclone threat. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how long any morning light easterly lasts at the beach.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed–Sat)
periods.pattern: Official weekly guidance expects instability and Pacific moisture to ramp from Thursday toward the weekend — humid, with early coastal rains possible and afternoon storms more widespread inland; still no tropical wave in the near term. Ensemble averages show a wetter pulse sometime midweek to weekend near Nicoya (timing disagrees: some means peak around Friday, others closer to next Sunday) with light-to-moderate or locally heavier daily totals, still cellular rather than a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Longer official outlook keeps Pacífico Norte quieter than peak rainy-season weeks (roughly 1–70 mm for 5–11 Oct). Marine winds: Tuesday night into Wednesday trend southwest about 10–15 kt; maps allow a brief weak easterly/northeast slot around Wednesday mornings before Pacific south–southwest flow reasserts later in the window. A new East Pacific low is likely to form south of southern Mexico mid–late week and drift west-northwest away from Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Keep midweek–weekend plans flexible for stronger storm days. Surf-wind quality: watch for a possible brief morning glass window around Wednesday if light easterlies win, then expect Pacific/onshore chop again later in the week. Nicaragua is not showing a clean all-day offshore quality signal — only a mild morning hint at best, not Nosara all-day offshore.
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued moist Pacífico Norte with a wetter midweek–weekend pulse; low–moderate on which day runs wettest and on how firmly any Wednesday easterly holds at beach hour.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from early into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for the current week. Ensemble means still allow moist days with pulses into mid-October (spread is high on which days), and the U.S. tropics outlook (updated 29 Sep, valid 7–20 Oct) still notes model support for a possible broader Central American rain-gyre pattern early in its week-2 window — worth watching, not locked in. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west; formation odds south of southern Mexico are now very high (~90%) through seven days.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes; re-check midweek if a gyre signal firms up or the Mexico-coast system draws more moisture south.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail and for any week-2 gyre risk past about a week.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only — elevated but not established
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No Costa Rica–centered gyre now. Watch midweek–weekend for a wetter Pacific-moisture pulse, and keep the broader week-2 (around Oct 7+) gyre mention from U.S. tropics guidance as a longer-range watch only — especially if the Mexico-coast low consolidates closer.
gyreWatch.supporting: Pacific moisture band remains active nearby. Ensemble means keep light-to-moderate Pacific-side rain with a wetter midweek–weekend pulse. Broad troughing and multi-center lows south of Mexico feed southwest monsoon flow. U.S. tropics outlook notes model support for a possible Central American gyre early in week-2. NHC shows a high chance of a new system forming off southern Mexico this week, which can enhance regional moisture even without a Costa Rica landfall.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No persistent closed low sits over Costa Rica on the main ensemble averages — the country often sits on the eastern fringe of Pacific troughing. Some midweek maps show higher pressure over northern Central America that breaks up a classic land-centered gyre. Official Sunday Pacífico Norte forecast is scattered/isolated showers, not a multi-day washout. Weekly outlook: no tropical waves the next few days. Longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico / Hawaii, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific / onshore dominant (light Papagayo E Sunday morning → S–SW Mon–Tue; brief weak E possible ~Wed mornings, then S–SW again)
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters (marine forecast issued Sun 1:29 a.m. PDT): Sunday morning northeasterly to easterly about 10 kt with scattered showers — light trade sniff only, not a strong all-day offshore. Overnight southeast about 10–15 kt; Monday south about 10–15 kt; Monday night light/variable then southeast to south Tuesday; Tuesday night into Wednesday southwest about 10–15 kt. Mid-level maps agree on Pacific west–southwest onshore early week, with a brief weak easterly/northeast slot around Wednesday mornings before south–southwest returns later. Do not read today’s light Papagayo easterly or midweek light/variable as glassy all-day offshore. Nicaragua: Caribbean trades exist offshore but means do not show clear all-day offshore on the Nica Pacific coast — only a mild morning-quality hint, not equal to Nosara all-day offshore.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early checks Sunday–Tuesday. Possible brief morning glass around Wednesday if light easterlies win — still not a clean all-day Caribbean-trade signal. Expect choppier Pacific/onshore–side flow most afternoons this period.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the marine forecast trend (light E Sunday → S–SW into midweek). Moderate on exact hour-to-hour beach winds and on how useful any Wednesday morning easterly window is.

whatChanged: Sunday official regional forecast softens yesterday’s sticky-weekend tone: partial humidity reduction and more isolated Pacífico Norte afternoon showers (Nicoya still ~35°C). Newest storm notice is now Sat 3 Oct 10:00 a.m. (active Pacific moisture band; afternoon storms; Pacific-coast rains may linger overnight). Genesis chance south of southern Mexico rises to ~90% in 7 days (was ~80%). Surf winds: Sunday confirms only a light morning easterly at Papagayo before the south–southwest onshore pattern; maps add a possible brief weak easterly slot around Wednesday mornings. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only but notes an elevated midweek–weekend wetter pulse.
practical: Best outdoors: Sunday morning before scattered afternoon storms; sticky heat continues. For surf, treat today through Tuesday as Pacific/onshore — early checks only; today’s light easterly is not all-day glass. Watch Wednesday mornings for a possible brief cleanup if light easterlies return. No tropical wave is lined up for the next few days. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline, but keep flexible midweek–weekend if the wetter pulse arrives. Latest official storm notice: Sat 3 Oct 10:00 a.m. — active Pacific moisture band; generally 20–40 mm with local 50–60 mm in favored mountain spots Saturday afternoon; soil saturation 85–95% flagged in parts of Zona Norte / Valle Central / Caribe Norte and Pacific mountain fringes.
